newsitem.title: USA: Kaczynski trial set for November 1997 - judge.
newsitem.headline: Kaczynski trial set for November 1997 - judge.

text.p: The trial of Unabomber suspect Theodore Kaczynski on charges of sending four bombs will begin on November 12 next year, a U.S. federal judge ruled on Friday.
U.S. District Judge Garland Burrell set the date at a hearing in Sacramento at which prosecutors argued for a May 1997 start to the trial and defence attorneys sought more time to study the evidence.
Kaczynski appeared in court for the first time since he was arraigned in Sacramento on June 25.
He was wearing a brown tweed jacket, his hair and beard were neatly cropped and he looked relaxed as he sat between his attorneys, chatting with them and smiling from time to time.
At the hearing, prosecutors and defence attorneys argued over dates for the filing of various pre-trial motions.

Burrell ruled that the defence must file its motion seeking to suppress evidence seized during the search of Kaczynski's Montana cabin by March 3, 1997, with a hearing on the issue to be held next May.
Kaczynski's attorneys have indicated that they will contest the validity of the warrant used in the search of the cabin, which the government said turned up a mass of evidence damaging to Kaczynski.
Kaczynski is accused of being the shadowy Unabomber who killed three people and injured 23 during an anti-technology bombing campaign between 1978 and 1995.
The former mathematics professor is charged with four bombings in Sacramento, two of them deadly. He has pleaded not guilty.
